title: Audit payload contract & SIEM integration playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for the team to: (1) define a stable audit payload contract for downstream consumers (SIEMs, GRC, forensic tooling), (2) document how RBAC v2 signals should appear in audit events, (3) describe evidence-automation hooks for sensitive-data actions, and (4) provide an incremental migration strategy from the current v1/v2 event variants to the proposed v3 contract.

High level goals / constraints:
- Consumers expect a predictable set of top-level fields for indexing and alerting: timestamp, event_id, tenant_id, actor_id, actor_type, action, resource_type, resource_id, outcome. Keep these always present.
- Backwards compatibility first: additive fields only where possible; deprecation windows with dual-write for 6 months.
- Privacy-by-default: PII must be redacted at source unless explicit consent/retention rules apply; events should include a redaction_reason code when fields are removed.
- Evidence automation must be co-owned with legal and SRE to ensure packaging, TTL and encryption meet retention and export rules.

Proposed canonical v3 audit payload (flattened contract, example keys):
- event_id: canonical uuid (string)
- timestamp: ISO-8601 UTC string
- tenant_id: org id (string)
- request_id: inbound request tracing id (string)
- actor_id: subject principal id (string)
- actor_type: user|service|api_key|system (string)
- actor_display_name: human name or service name (string, nullable)
- actor_ip: client ip if available (string, redacted/pseudonymize in prod)
- role_ids: comma-separated role ids effective for action (string)
- role_grant_origin: direct|group|policy|inheritance (string)
- rbac_version: v2 (or v2.1 when rolled out) (string)
- action: verb-like action e.g., session.create, model.deploy, policy.update (string)
- resource_type: e.g., model, deployment, key, project, audit_config (string)
- resource_id: canonical resource id (string)
- outcome: success|failure|denied|partial (string)
- latency_ms: integer as string (string)
- token_cost: token count or cost unit (string)
- policy_evaluation: pass|fail|warning (string)
- policy_ids: comma-separated policy ids referenced (string)
- evidence_refs: comma-separated artifact ids produced for this event (string)
- encryption_key_id: KMS key id used for evidence packaging (string)
- retention_ttl_days: integer as string (string)
- ingest_version: v3 (string)
- raw_payload_preview: short base64 (<=1024 chars) or null (string, optional)
- schema_version: single semantic version string to drive consumer logic (e.g., 3.0.0)

Notes on specific fields:
- role_ids/role_grant_origin: RBAC v2 has transient and derived grants (e.g., group membership). We record the effective role_ids plus where grant came from so auditors can reconstruct.
- evidence_refs: references to artifacts created by evidence-automation (see section below). These are IDs that map to encrypted bundles in the evidence store.
- raw_payload_preview: only present for non-sensitive flows and limited to a size budget. Will be null for calls flagged as sensitive.

Examples (toy event line):
{
  "event_id": "9f3b2e3a-6d2e-4f6d-a4e3-1a2b3c4d5e6f",
  "timestamp": "2025-01-10T14:22:07Z",
  "tenant_id": "org_88F3",
  "request_id": "req_7a8b9c",
  "actor_id": "user_123",
  "actor_type": "user",
  "actor_display_name": "maria@acme.com",
  "actor_ip": "redacted",
  "role_ids": "role_admin,role_model_ops",
  "role_grant_origin": "policy",
  "rbac_version": "v2",
  "action": "model.deploy",
  "resource_type": "model",
  "resource_id": "mdl_42",
  "outcome": "success",
  "latency_ms": "342",
  "token_cost": "0",
  "policy_evaluation": "pass",
  "policy_ids": "policy_11",
  "evidence_refs": "ev_20250110_0001",
  "encryption_key_id": "kms-prod-us-east-1-key-23",
  "retention_ttl_days": "90",
  "ingest_version": "v3",
  "raw_payload_preview": null,
  "schema_version": "3.0.0"
}

SIEM export mapping guidance (Splunk/Elastic/QRadar):
- Index-time fields: event_id, timestamp, tenant_id, actor_id, actor_type, action, resource_type, resource_id, outcome. Keep these keywords for alerts.
- Enrichers: Add geo from actor_ip (if not redacted). Map tenant_id -> customer.name for dashboards.
- Use schema_version and ingest_version to route to parsing rules in ingest cluster.
- Sensitive markers: Add a boolean tag sensitive=true for events that triggered evidence automation. SIEM rules should escalate these to a higher retention/alerting tier.

Evidence automation playbook (for actions that touch protected data or privileged ops):
- Triggers: any policy_evaluation != pass, actions on keys (kms.*), exports (data.download), high privilege role changes (role.create, role.assign), model weight exports.
- Package: collect request headers, request/response digests, snapshot of effective RBAC (role_ids + grant_origin), related request_ids, execution trace (span ids) and a checksum. Create encrypted artifact, store reference in evidence_refs.
- Ownership: evidence store owned by compliance; SRE provides lifecycle (encryption, replication). Legal sets retention_ttl_days per artifact.
- Access: access to evidence artifacts requires approval flow; all accesses emit an evidence.access.audit event.

Migration strategy (v1/v2 -> v3):
1) Define canonical field mapping table (done).
2) Implement server-side dual-write option: current event format + v3 payload in parallel for 6 months under feature flag.
3) Roll out parsers/adapters for downstream consumers (splunk indexers, external SIEM integrations). Provide a consumer shim library (audit-shim) with transformation helpers.
4) After consumer readiness, flip single-write to v3 and keep compat adapter for 3 months to replay missed events.
5) Deprecate old fields with a 9 month notice and final removal.

Operational runbook snippets:
- If SIEM parsing drops events: check ingest_version mismatch -> ensure index parser updated; max event size policy in router may have truncated raw_payload_preview.
- If evidence packaging fails: fallback is to emit an event with evidence_error_reason and mark evidence_refs as "pending". Do NOT drop the core audit event.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Standardize numeric field types: we store latency_ms and token_cost as strings to avoid downstream schema breaks. Should we instead enforce integer? (ops/analytics to decide)
- role_ids as comma-separated string is convenient but brittle. Consider array-of-strings for downstream ES mapping; requires consumers to accept arrays.
- Redaction policy: per-tenant opt-in for raw_payload_preview? Legal to confirm.
- SIEM export throughput: need benchmarks for large orgs (~10k req/s). Engineering to provide expected event QPS and cost estimate.
- Evidence TTL defaults per classification level (sensitive, restricted, public). Legal to enumerate.

References and links:
- CONFLUENCE-SEC-4567: RBAC v2 design doc (link above)
- JIRA-AUDIT-112: consumer readiness epic
- audit-shim repo PRs for adapter code.

Appendix: Short checklist for a release of v3 audit contract:
- [ ] Finalize canonical field names and types with analytics and infra.
- [ ] Implement dual-write with feature flag in serving runtime.
- [ ] Publish updated ingest parsers to internal ES/Splunk clusters.
- [ ] Ship audit-shim v0.1 library and announce to partners.
- [ ] Run consumer compatibility sweep, collect errors, iterate.
- [ ] Agree retention defaults and evidence access process with legal.

Notes to self (work-in-progress style):
- Want to avoid deeply nested event.context blobs; keep everything flattenable for Elastic. If we must embed JSON, include base64-encoded compressed blob and explicit preview fields.
- Check with SRE about Kafka topic naming for audit-v3 vs audit-v2 (we may reuse topic but add header ingest_version).
- Slack threads: #sec-audit, #sre-observability -> ping Marcus for ingest benchmark numbers.

This document is intentionally informal and drafty; use it as the working contract while we iterate toward a final spec.
